                    ### Question
                    An investigator studying the immunologic profile of various cells notices that the blood of a test subject agglutinates upon addition of a serum containing antibodies against P blood group antigens. Infection with which of the following pathogens would most likely be prevented by these antibodies?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Parvovirus B19
opb. Babesia microti
opc. Plasmodium vivax
opd. Epstein Barr virus
ope. Influenza virus

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Antibodies against P blood group antigens are likely to prevent infection by Parvovirus B19, as it uses the P antigen for cell entry. These antibodies would not prevent infections by Babesia microti, Plasmodium vivax, Epstein Barr virus, or Influenza virus, as these pathogens do not utilize the P antigen.
